This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State-Opposite Party.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with G.R. Case No.1400 of 2023, arising out of Bentakar (42 Mouza) P.S.
Case No.402 of 2023, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C.-IV, Cuttack for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 420/294/506 of the I.P.C.
4.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that earlier this matter was not before any other Bench of this Court.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner was earlier before this Court in BLAPL No.1385 of 2024.

He further submitted that pursuant to the order dated 18.03.2024, the petitioner was directed to be released on bail subject to the Petitioner refunding a sum of Rs.60,000/- at the time of his release on bail and the balance amount of Rs.1,20,000/- shall be refunded in the equal four monthly instalments.
He further submitted that since the Petitioner could not refund the aforesaid monthly equal instalments, an NBW was issued against the present Petitioner, since now the petitioner is in jail custody.
In such view of the matter, it is submitted that the Petitioner is ready and willing to refund the balanced amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, in the event he grants some time to refund the balanced amount.

1 5.
Learned Additional Standing Counsel on the other hand opposed the bail application of the Petitioner on the ground that the Petitioner was earlier released on bail.
Further submitted that in the event the Petitioner is released on bail, he might indulge in similar criminal offences.

Therefore,
on such ground, learned counsel for the State submitted that the bail application of the Petitioner be rejected at this juncture.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and on careful consideration of the surrounding facts as well as materials on record, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail subject to imposition of stringent conditions.
7. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on previous bail bond.

Release of the petitioner shall also be subject to a condition that the Petitioner shall now refund the balanced amount of Rs.1,20,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Twenty Thousands) within a period of six months.
Failing which it is open to the learned court below to take coercive action against the Petitioner and take back him into jail custody.
8. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge Anil Location: High Court of Orissa Gudu @ Nihar Ranjan Parida vs State Of Odisha .....
